_note: Bitcoin Ecosystem directory (handovers bitcoin-ecosystem.md + ecosystem-fixes.md, 22 Oct 2026). Built by seo-build/ecosystem.mjs. Structure, links and entries live here; all page text lives in ecosystem-strings/<lang>.json. Entries (names, verdicts, tags) stay English in every language. Every URL was checked by hand; re-check before changing 'reviewed'.

entries.name: The Bitcoin whitepaper
entries.verdict: Satoshi Nakamoto's nine-page original from 2008. Short, readable and still the best primary source.

entries.name: Bitcoin for Everybody (Saylor Academy)
entries.verdict: A free, self-paced beginner course with readings and a final exam. Good if you like structure.

entries.name: Plan ₿ Network
entries.verdict: Free structured courses from first steps to advanced topics, available in many European languages.

entries.name: 21 Lessons
entries.verdict: Gigi's short essays on what Bitcoin teaches about money, technology and philosophy. Free to read online.

entries.name: Satoshi Nakamoto Institute
entries.verdict: The archive of Satoshi's emails and forum posts, plus the economic and cryptographic writing Bitcoin grew out of.

entries.name: Lopp's Bitcoin resources
entries.verdict: Jameson Lopp's large, regularly updated index of Bitcoin information. Best used as a reference, not a starting point.

entries.name: 21ideas
entries.verdict: Translations of essential bitcoin essays and guides for Russian-speaking readers.

entries.name: Learn Me A Bitcoin
entries.verdict: Clear, illustrated explanations of how transactions, keys and blocks work under the hood.

entries.name: The Bitcoin Standard (Saifedean Ammous)
entries.verdict: The classic case for Bitcoin as sound money, told through the history of money. Opinionated and influential.

entries.name: Broken Money (Lyn Alden)
entries.verdict: A calm, well-researched history of money and banking that ends with Bitcoin. The best pick for sceptical readers.

entries.name: The Fiat Standard (Saifedean Ammous)
entries.verdict: The companion to The Bitcoin Standard: how the current money system works and what it costs.

entries.name: Layered Money (Nik Bhatia)
entries.verdict: A short, clear explanation of how money is built in layers, from gold to central banks to Bitcoin and Lightning.

entries.name: The Price of Tomorrow (Jeff Booth)
entries.verdict: Why technology pushes prices down while the monetary system fights it. Not a Bitcoin book first, but a strong argument for one.

entries.name: The Bullish Case for Bitcoin (Vijay Boyapati)
entries.verdict: The famous essay expanded into a book: why Bitcoin could become a global store of value, step by step.

entries.name: Mastering Bitcoin (Antonopoulos, Harding)
entries.verdict: The standard technical reference for developers and curious engineers. Free to read on GitHub.

entries.name: Grokking Bitcoin (Kalle Rosenbaum)
entries.verdict: A gentle, illustrated walk through how Bitcoin works, written by a Swedish developer. Free on GitHub.

entries.name: What Bitcoin Did
entries.verdict: Long-form interviews from the UK on markets, politics and people in Bitcoin. A good weekly habit.

entries.name: TFTC
entries.verdict: Marty Bent's show and newsletter on Bitcoin, energy and the wider economy. Opinionated and frequent.

entries.name: Bitcoin Audible
entries.verdict: Guy Swann reads the best Bitcoin essays aloud and discusses them. Ideal if you prefer listening to reading.

entries.name: Stephan Livera Podcast
entries.verdict: Technical and economic deep dives with developers and builders. Best for listeners who want depth.

entries.name: Citadel Dispatch
entries.verdict: Matt Odell's live show on privacy, self-custody and freedom tech. Practical and frank.

entries.name: Bitcoin Fundamentals (The Investor's Podcast)
entries.verdict: Investor-oriented conversations on Bitcoin's place in a portfolio and the macro picture.

entries.name: Einundzwanzig
entries.verdict: The leading German-language Bitcoin podcast, run by a community from Germany, Austria and Switzerland.

entries.name: Fountain
entries.verdict: A podcast app with Lightning built in, so you can send sats directly to the shows you value.

entries.name: BTC Sessions
entries.verdict: Patient, step-by-step tutorials on Bitcoin and Lightning tools. The best channel for practical first steps.

entries.name: Bitcoin Magazine
entries.verdict: Conference talks, interviews and news from the largest Bitcoin media brand.

entries.name: Plan ₿ Network
entries.verdict: Recorded courses and conference talks from the Swiss-based education project, many in European languages.

entries.name: BTC Prague
entries.verdict: Talks from Europe's largest Bitcoin conference. Useful if you could not attend in person.

entries.name: Ministry of Nodes
entries.verdict: UK-based guides to running your own node and taking responsibility for your own Bitcoin.

entries.name: Simply Bitcoin
entries.verdict: A daily live show on Bitcoin news and adoption. Light in tone, consistent in schedule.

entries.name: The Bitcoin Layer
entries.verdict: Nik Bhatia's analysis of bonds, rates and macro through a Bitcoin lens. For readers of Layered Money.

entries.name: Natalie Brunell
entries.verdict: A former journalist interviewing economists and builders in an accessible way. Good for newcomers.

entries.name: God Bless Bitcoin
entries.verdict: A feature-length documentary on Bitcoin, money and faith. A thoughtful watch for a family evening.

entries.name: Bitcoin Amsterdam
entries.verdict: Two days of talks and networking in Amsterdam, with a strong business and institutional track.

entries.name: Swiss Bitcoin Conference
entries.verdict: A bitcoin-only weekend on Lake Constance with a community feel and talks in German and English.

entries.name: BTC Prague
entries.verdict: Europe's largest bitcoin-only conference: three days, several stages and a large expo.

entries.name: Bitcoin FilmFest
entries.verdict: A film festival about Bitcoin and freedom, with screenings, panels and a relaxed crowd.

entries.name: BTCHEL
entries.verdict: The Nordic Bitcoin conference. The organisers have not yet confirmed the 2027 dates.

entries.name: Baltic Honeybadger
entries.verdict: One of Europe's longest-running bitcoin-only conferences, known for technical depth and a hacker spirit.

entries.name: Bitcoin Core
entries.verdict: Running your own node means your wallet no longer reveals your addresses to someone else's server.

entries.name: Tor Project
entries.verdict: Hides your IP address when browsing or when your node talks to the network. Free and widely audited.

entries.name: Tails
entries.verdict: A portable operating system that runs from a USB stick and leaves no trace on the computer.

entries.name: Mullvad VPN
entries.verdict: A Swedish VPN that needs no email to sign up and accepts bitcoin. Simple, honest pricing.

entries.name: Proton
entries.verdict: Encrypted email and storage from Switzerland. Paid plans can be settled in bitcoin.

entries.name: Silent Payments
entries.verdict: A reusable payment code that avoids address reuse when people pay you. Overview of the standard and supporting tools.

entries.name: Payjoin
entries.verdict: A payment technique in which sender and receiver both contribute inputs, breaking common chain-analysis assumptions.

entries.name: Bitcoiner.guide privacy
entries.verdict: A practical guide to everyday privacy habits for bitcoiners, from address reuse to KYC data.

entries.name: Bitcoin Wiki: Privacy
entries.verdict: The most thorough reference on how Bitcoin privacy works and where it leaks. Dense but authoritative.

entries.name: BTC Map
entries.verdict: A community-maintained map of places that accept bitcoin, with many European cities covered.

entries.name: Bitrefill
entries.verdict: Gift cards and phone top-ups for thousands of European brands, payable with bitcoin and Lightning.

entries.name: The Bitcoin Company
entries.verdict: Gift cards paid in bitcoin, with sats back on everyday purchases.

entries.name: Lugano's Plan ₿
entries.verdict: The Swiss city programme where hundreds of shops and the city itself accept bitcoin. A model for Europe.

entries.name: Proton
entries.verdict: Pay for encrypted email, calendar and storage with bitcoin.

entries.name: Mullvad VPN
entries.verdict: A VPN subscription you can pay in bitcoin without giving an email address.

entries.name: Njalla
entries.verdict: Domain names and servers with a privacy focus, payable in bitcoin.

entries.name: 1984 Hosting
entries.verdict: Icelandic web hosting and domains with a long free-speech record, payable in bitcoin.

entries.name: BTCPay Server
entries.verdict: The free, self-hosted standard for accepting bitcoin. No fees and no middleman, with plugins for most shops.

entries.name: Swiss Bitcoin Pay
entries.verdict: Lightning payments for shops and restaurants from Switzerland, with a simple point-of-sale app.

entries.name: Coinsnap
entries.verdict: A German Lightning payment service with plugins for WooCommerce and other shop systems.

entries.name: Bitcoinize
entries.verdict: Ready-made point-of-sale terminals for accepting Lightning payments at the counter.

entries.name: OpenNode
entries.verdict: A hosted bitcoin payment processor with an API and e-commerce integrations.

entries.name: Zaprite
entries.verdict: Invoicing and checkout that settles to your own wallet. Good for freelancers and B2B.

entries.name: LNbits
entries.verdict: Free, open-source Lightning accounts and extensions, including point-of-sale and paywalls.

entries.name: Voltage
entries.verdict: Managed Lightning node infrastructure for businesses that do not want to run servers themselves.

entries.name: Bitcoin Dev Kit (BDK)
entries.verdict: A modern Rust library for building on-chain wallets, with bindings for mobile and other languages.

entries.name: Lightning Dev Kit (LDK)
entries.verdict: A flexible Lightning implementation as a library, for teams that want Lightning inside their own app.

entries.name: Breez SDK
entries.verdict: Add self-custodial Lightning payments to an app with a few calls.

entries.name: Bitcoin Core
entries.verdict: The reference implementation. Its RPC interface and documentation are the base of most Bitcoin software.

entries.name: Core Lightning
entries.verdict: A modular, plugin-friendly Lightning node implementation.

entries.name: ACINQ (Eclair, Phoenix)
entries.verdict: The Paris-based team behind the Eclair node and the Lightning tooling that powers Phoenix.

entries.name: Polar
entries.verdict: Spin up local Lightning test networks in one click. The fastest way to prototype.

entries.name: Bitcoin Optech
entries.verdict: The weekly technical newsletter that tracks protocol changes. Required reading for teams shipping Bitcoin software.

entries.name: mempool.space
entries.verdict: Open-source block explorer software and API that you can self-host for your own stack.

entries.name: Bitcoin Stack Exchange
entries.verdict: Questions and answers from protocol developers. Search here before you ask.

entries.name: Bitcoiner Jobs
entries.verdict: The main job board for bitcoin-only companies, with many remote and European roles across all functions.

entries.name: Brink
entries.verdict: London-based non-profit that funds and mentors Bitcoin Core developers through grants and fellowships.

entries.name: OpenSats
entries.verdict: Grants and long-term support for open-source Bitcoin developers and projects.

entries.name: HRF Bitcoin Development Fund
entries.verdict: Grants from the Human Rights Foundation for privacy and usability work on Bitcoin.

entries.name: Spiral
entries.verdict: Grants and full-time open-source work on Bitcoin and Lightning, funded by Block.

entries.name: ₿OSS Challenge (Chaincode)
entries.verdict: A free training programme for aspiring Bitcoin open-source developers, run by Chaincode Labs.

entries.name: Summer of Bitcoin
entries.verdict: A paid summer internship for university students working on Bitcoin open-source projects.

entries.name: The Bitcoin Dev Project
entries.verdict: Curated paths and good first issues to start contributing to Bitcoin open source.

entries.name: bitcoin-only.com
entries.verdict: The long-running directory of bitcoin-only tools and resources that inspired this section.

entries.name: Bitcoiner.guide
entries.verdict: Clear, opinionated guides on self-custody, privacy and running your own infrastructure.

entries.name: Plan ₿ Network
entries.verdict: Swiss-based open education platform translating Bitcoin courses into dozens of languages.

entries.name: Einundzwanzig
entries.verdict: The German-speaking Bitcoin community behind a podcast, education material and open-source tools.

entries.name: 21ideas
entries.verdict: A volunteer project translating Bitcoin essays and guides for Russian-speaking readers.

entries.name: PlebNet
entries.verdict: A community of Lightning node operators sharing knowledge on running routing nodes.

entries.name: Bitcoin Design
entries.verdict: An open community of designers improving the usability of Bitcoin products, with a free design guide.

entries.name: Satoshi Nakamoto Institute
entries.verdict: Preserves the history and literature of Bitcoin, from Satoshi's writing to the cypherpunks before him.
